question: Are new fixed-FY profit revision events preceded by industry price moves, followed by new excess returns, or both?
estimand: industry price around observed broker report revisions; not an industry consensus factor and not a capacity-constrained strategy
scope: R11 locally cached selected reports, profit_cny only, same stock/broker/explicit FY; FY=publication year+1 main; L2/L3 separately
events: each unique stock/broker/FY/publication date; simultaneous unequal values invalid; predecessor is immediately preceding observed date, <=365 days; do not skip invalid predecessor; signed symmetric revision, zero stays flat
timing: signal = first exchange session strictly after proxy publication date; prior window ends prior session; reaction=signal close/prior close; entry next session close; post20/60 from entry; no same-day claim
mapping: signal prior-calendar-month historical membership, no current membership; median brokers within company, then median companies per industry/signal date/FY; denominator and simultaneous-event firms retained
windows: pre20/pre60 ending signal-1; reaction1; post20 main/post60 secondary from signal+1; require full continuous basket block, unknown not zero
comparators: all industry-date price contexts; exact era/level/signal date; prior20 excess quintiles formed without outcomes; non-event industries in same quintile with >=3 complete controls; report pre60, reaction and future; no replacement or averaging incomplete controls
aggregation: up/down/flat; industry-event means and date-equal means separately, dates/industries/year coverage; FY and hierarchy overlap disclosed
inference: descriptive mechanism timing audit, not causal inference or predictive acceptance; no threshold optimization; no new positive model claim
limitations: selected monthly-latest archived reports are not complete broker event history
not all revisions within365 days are observed; predecessor means previous cached report
publication clock reconstructed from body/list; archived2026-10
matching prior20 only does not control all style, fundamentals or anticipation
